body: Do we really need a new file for this? It appears to be used only in 1 place (outside of a test that feels redundant), so why not just type the code there?

I'm not sure how useful it is to have the distinction between constraint space and body space. Jolt provides 'constraint space' functions because it gives the lowest level of access, but I expect most people to not understand constraint space (and I don't think Godot offers an easy way of getting the constraint space in the first place, but I might be mistaken). I would expect people to always reason about body space instead and I would only offer that interface.

See my other comment: I think this can be hidden from the user. Even if the joint has been configured using Euler angles the `get_angular_target_rotation` could just return a sensible quaternion. This means users don't need to reason about this and it can always return body space.
I would probably put this code inside `_update_spring_equilibrium` and have a switch there
Not sure why this enum needs to be repeated

I don't think this is true. Euler angles have a concept of CW and CCW but quaternions don't. I took the liberty of updating your sample: [jolt-angular-target-demo2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27307396/jolt-angular-target-demo2.zip). I changed:

* `set_angular_target_rotation_cs` -> `set_angular_target_rotation`
* Removed `EULER_PIVOT` / `QUAT_PIVOT` and replaced them with the actual anchor bodies
* Gave both the anchors and the joints a rotation to ensure that there is a difference between anchor space and world space and that there is a difference between anchor space and constraint space.

If I run this with your current code it looks like this:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c78caa45-0a17-4d24-955d-3412452e63a8

If I remove the `Conjugate()` it looks like this:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cbec303a-c046-4d79-9cd8-1b8d3f1439e3

(Note that I didn't bother to fix the Euler path - blue box)

`angular_target_rotation` is in body space, `Basis::from_euler(...)` will return a value in constraint space. I think you need to forward the call to the physics server and for Jolt return:

```
(to_godot(constraint->GetConstraintToBody1Matrix()) * Basis::from_euler(...)).get_quaternion()
```
Note that Quaternions have the concept of 6 intrinsic and 6 extrinsic euler order equivilents.
